question: An article was sold for ₹1,225 after allowing a discount of 12.5%. If 9.5% discount is given, then for how much will it be sold?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Let the MP be 100, Discount = 12.5 then SP = 100 - 12.5 = 87.5

MP = 1225/87.5 × 100 = 1400

Discount = 1400 × 9.5% = 133

SP = MP - Discount

SP = 1400 - 133 = **Rs.1267**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

An article was sold for Rs 1225 after allowing a discount of 12.5%

If 9.5% discount is given then how much will it be sold

**Formula used:**

SP = **(MP)/(100)(100 - D) **

SP = MP - Discount

SP = Selling price, MP = Marked price, & D = Discount

**Calculation:**

SP = (MP)/(100)(100 - D)

⇒ (MP)/(100) (100 - 12.5) ​​ = 1225

⇒ (MP)/(100)(87.5) = 1225

⇒ MP = 1400

Now, If the discount is 9.5% then, 

SP = (1400)/(100)(100 - 9.5)

⇒ SP = 14× 90.5

⇒ SP = 1267

**∴ An article was sold for ₹1267 after allowing a discount of 9.5%.**
